narrative: Today's refresh caught a real data-integrity anomaly, investigated in depth before publishing: the relay's own custody endpoint briefly reported a negative surplus (WPRL supply exceeding locked PRL by ~28,800 PRL). Cross-checked independently — the WPRL contract's on-chain total supply was confirmed byte-for-byte via a direct Ethereum RPC call, and prlscan's independent read of the lock address's own balance (built from its own received/sent transaction ledger) shows ~38,900 PRL more than the relay's custody figure, with no single large transaction in the address's recent history that would explain a real shortfall. That points to a bug or stale field in the relay's own lockGrains calculation rather than an actual funding gap, but it isn't fully resolved, so TVL/surplus fields are nulled this run rather than publishing a number in either direction. Separately: price continued easing (-7.6%, second down day in a row, no identified catalyst), network difficulty keeps its gentle decline, and GitHub/social were otherwise quiet.

anomalies: Relay custody data flagged and left null this run pending investigation. /api/custody reported a negative surplus (custody ~28,800 PRL below minted WPRL supply), driven entirely by the lock address's reported balance (lockGrains: 45,888.62 PRL). Independently verified minted_wprl above via a direct eth_call to the WPRL contract's totalSupply() — it matches the relay's own totalSupplyGrains exactly (979,092.94 PRL), so the supply side is solid. But prlscan's own ledger for the same lock address (received_grains minus sent_grains, self-consistent) shows a balance of 84,787.52 PRL — about 38,900 PRL higher than the relay reports — and the address's last 30 transactions are all small routine deposit-sweeps and fee-consolidations, nothing that would account for a real ~39k PRL outflow. Most likely a stale or buggy field in the relay's own custody rollup rather than an actual shortfall, but this needs relay-team confirmation before either number is trusted, so tvl_prl/tvl_usd/surplus_prl/surplus_pct are null here rather than published as fact in either direction.

incidents.summary: Pearl's July 1 MoE (mixture-of-experts) PoW extension had an economic-pricing bug: sparse expert-routed proofs were credited as full dense-difficulty work, letting miners claim outsized rewards without proportional real compute (not proof forgery, no PearlBridge custody impact, and DeFiLlama's hack database lists nothing for Pearl). Reported network hashrate rose from ~30 EH/s to 90+ EH/s over three weeks as this was exploited. The core team activated a dense-only PoW fork at mainnet height ~91,630 to shut off MoE crediting, with a same-day hotfix for a template-classification bug in the fork logic itself. Current chain height (91,737) is past the fork — the fix is live.

MinePRL, the canonical community pool tracked by this dashboard, is offline (site redirects visitors to prlscan.com); exact offline date within the past ~6 weeks is unconfirmed. Network hashrate and pool worker-count fields are null this snapshot pending a replacement public data source.

The bridge relay's /api/custody endpoint briefly reported a negative surplus (WPRL supply ~28,800 PRL above locked PRL), driven by its lockGrains field reading well below an independent read of the same address. WPRL total supply was independently confirmed correct via a direct Ethereum RPC call to the contract's totalSupply(). prlscan's own ledger for the lock address (received minus sent, self-consistent) put its balance about 38,900 PRL higher than the relay reported, and no single recent transaction in that address's history explains a real shortfall of that size — pointing to a bug or stale field in the relay's custody rollup rather than an actual funding gap. TVL and surplus fields are null in this snapshot pending relay-side confirmation; not treated as a confirmed incident, but flagged here for visibility and follow-up.
